problem_statement: hakimov-dev/landing-template (landing-template) is a Nuxt 2 Tailwind marketing landing template built statically with nuxt generate and served from dist/ across the home (/), pricing (/pricing) and customers (/customers) routes. The site needs a shared 'Launch readiness' rail that summarises the product's operational footprint (live regions, average deploy time, uptime SLA, support hours) as four metric tiles and that appears consistently on the home, pricing AND customers surfaces so the 'ship with confidence across every plan' story holds across the whole site. The rail's tile row must lay out responsively so the document never overflows horizontally on mobile, and it must keep the site's light brand palette (white surface, pink/gold accents) rather than an off-brand dark slab. On the home surface the rail also exposes a 'Coverage by region' filter whose readout must update on every chip click to reflect the active selection (e.g. 'Showing: EU - 15 live' after clicking the EU chip).
required_content: A shared 'Launch readiness' rail (a new components/LaunchRail.vue rendered from the default layout) appears on the home, pricing AND customers routes, summarising the product as four metric tiles (Live regions, Avg. deploy time, Uptime SLA, Support hours).
The rail's four-tile row wraps responsively so the whole document never overflows horizontally on mobile (documentElement scrollWidth stays within the viewport, tolerance 24px).
The rail keeps the landing template's light brand palette (white surface, pink/gold accents, indigo title) so it matches the surrounding marketing sections rather than an off-brand dark card.

On the home surface the rail's 'Coverage by region' filter exposes a live readout that updates on every chip click: after clicking the EU chip it reads 'Showing: EU - 15 live', reflecting the active region rather than the initial 'All regions' snapshot.
The existing Nuxt routes, the hero, About, Call-to-Action and footer sections, the nav (Home / Customers / Pricing), and the template's assets all stay intact (no regressions).
design_constraints: Reuse the template's own local assets (the hero and github artwork under assets/imgs, emitted to /_nuxt/img) and the existing Tailwind marketing styling; introduce no external or remote media.
The shared rail must be a single component rendered from the default layout on the whitelisted surfaces so its cross-page presence is consistent; do not duplicate divergent copies per page.
Keep the rail's four tiles on a wrapping row (flex-wrap) with a fluid basis so mobile never overflows; do not pin the tile row to a fixed pixel width.
The region-filter readout must be computed live from the clicked region, not a value snapshotted once at component setup.
state_constraints: desktop_contact captures the landing1 page scrolled to the contact flow on a 1440px desktop: the four-step landing contact flow strip lays out its steps in a row above the contact form and every step card is readable.
mobile_contact captures the same contact flow at 390px, where the baseline fixed-width nowrap step row overflows the viewport and forces the landing1 document into horizontal scrolling.
tablet_landing captures the landing1 page at 834px as an intermediate viewport where the step strip is comfortably within tolerance.
desktop_landing and mobile_landing capture the full landing1 page; mobile_landing is where the baseline strip's horizontal overflow is observed at 390px.

Source inspection confirms the contact flow is a self-contained section component (src/home/sections/ContactFlow1.jsx) whose step-strip layout lives in that file, so the responsive fix is isolated to that component's strip styles.

change_completion: The 'Launch readiness' rail renders on the home, pricing and customers routes with its four metric tiles and grounded copy.
The region-filter readout updates to 'Showing: EU - 15 live' after the EU chip is clicked, reflecting the live selection.
design_consistency: The rail keeps the template's light brand palette (white surface, pink/gold accents) rather than an off-brand dark slab, matching the reference visually.
The rail reuses the template's own assets and the existing Tailwind layout, and the hero, About, Call-to-Action and footer sections stay intact.
responsive: The rail's tile row wraps on mobile so the document does not overflow horizontally beyond the 24px tolerance on mobile_rail_home.
The home hero and rail remain usable across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.
regression: The 'Main Hero Message to sell yourself!' hero copy and the nav remain present so the site chrome stays intact.
The pricing and customers routes still render their own headings with the shared rail beneath them.

author_notes: L4-hardened design-continuity task on hakimov-dev/landing-template (the landing-template Nuxt 2 marketing site): the shared launch-readiness rail is the vehicle for four orthogonal gates. D6 (no_horizontal_overflow) is measured on mobile_rail_home where the rail is present in all legs, so the tile row's responsive layout is the sole discriminator; D3 (visual_regression) compares the rail's home render against the reference light-brand palette; D2 (dom_assertions) checks the rail's cross-surface presence on the pricing and customers routes; D4 (interaction_assertions) checks the region-filter readout updates live after clicking the EU chip. The rail reuses the template's own local assets and Tailwind styling. The baseline reproduces the original layout defect (a fixed-width non-wrapping tile row) and drops the rail from the pricing and customers surfaces, so it fails D6/D3/D2 but keeps a correct region filter and passes D4; the bad solution is a smart-wrong restyle that additionally repaints the rail as an off-brand dark slab and freezes the readout, so it fails all four gates.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: hakimov-dev/landing-template is a runnable Nuxt 2 Tailwind marketing landing template with a real multi-route structure (home / pricing / customers) and a shared default layout, an ideal host for an L4 design-continuity task that adds a shared cross-surface launch-readiness rail (D2/D3/D6) and wires a live region-filter readout (D4).
